title: THE PLAN BACKFIRED.
paragraphs: THE PLAN BACKFIRED.

One moment, Haman stood at the peak of power.
The next moment, he stood at the edge of the very gallows he built.
History records many stories of powerful people falling—but Esther 7 is different. This is not just political drama. This is not merely palace intrigue.
This is divine reversal.
And if you read the moment carefully, you can almost feel the tension in the room.

The king is seated.
The wine is poured.
Queen Esther has waited for the perfect moment.
For days she carried a secret that could cost her life.

Because the decree was already written.
A nation was already marked for death.
And the architect of the genocide was sitting comfortably at the king’s table.
His name was Haman.

Powerful.
Respected.
Feared.
But underneath the polished robes and royal favor lived a heart poisoned by pride and hatred.
One man had wounded his ego—Mordecai.
Mordecai refused to bow.
That small act of quiet conviction ignited something dark in Haman’s soul. Pride turned into rage. Rage turned into a plot. And the plot turned into a decree that would wipe out an entire people.
Not just Mordecai.
Every Jew.

Men.
Women.
Children.
Haman built the trap carefully. Strategically. Politically. He manipulated the king. He engineered the law. He even constructed a 75-foot gallows meant specifically for Mordecai.
He thought he was writing the final chapter.
But heaven was already writing a reversal.
Because while Haman was building gallows…
God was positioning Esther.
A young Jewish woman placed in a palace for such a time as this.

And when the moment came, Esther did not scream.
She did not accuse recklessly.
She did not react in fear.
She spoke truth with courage.

“If I have found favor in your sight, O king… let my life be granted me for my wish, and my people for my request. For we have been sold… to be destroyed, to be killed, and to be annihilated.” — Esther 7:3–4
The room froze.
The king’s face hardened.
“Who is he? Where is he?” the king demanded.
Then Esther pointed directly at the man sitting beside them.
“The adversary and enemy is this wicked Haman.” — Esther 7:6
In that instant, the powerful man became a terrified one.
The mask fell.
The scheme was exposed.
And suddenly the gallows he prepared for another man became the instrument of his own downfall.
“So they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai.” — Esther 7:10
The plan backfired.
This is one of the clearest pictures in Scripture of how God overturns injustice.
Evil may rise high.
But it never rises above the throne of God.
Some of you reading this know what it feels like to face a “Haman moment.”

Someone tried to ruin your reputation.
Someone manipulated the truth about you.
Someone quietly built a trap behind your back.

Maybe it happened at work.
Maybe it happened in family.
Maybe even inside church circles.
You felt powerless.
You wondered if truth would ever be seen.
Esther 7 reminds us of something powerful:
God sees the hidden schemes.
Nothing escapes His sight.

Not the whispered lies.
Not the secret manipulation.
Not the pride that thinks it can outplay heaven.

The proud build gallows for others…
but pride always builds the platform for its own fall.
Yet this story points to something even deeper.
Because the Bible tells an even greater story of a plan that backfired.
When Jesus was arrested, mocked, beaten, and crucified, the powers of darkness believed they had finally won.
Satan thought the Messiah was defeated.
Sin believed it had silenced righteousness.
Death believed it had closed the final chapter.

The cross looked like humiliation.
It looked like injustice.
It looked like defeat.
But just like in Esther…
God was writing a reversal.
Three days later, the stone rolled away.
Jesus rose from the grave.

What looked like defeat became victory.
What looked like shame became glory.
What looked like death became salvation.
The greatest backfire in history happened at the cross.
Because the very instrument meant to destroy Christ became the doorway through which sinners like us could be saved.
Through Jesus, God reverses more than injustice.
He reverses us.

From guilty to forgiven.
From rebels to redeemed.
From condemned to children of God.
That is the real message behind Esther’s courage and Haman’s fall.
God is not absent when evil rises.
He is working behind the scenes, preparing a moment when truth is revealed and justice stands.
And if you are walking through a season where it feels like wickedness is winning…
Hold on.
God specializes in reversals.
The trap may be set.
But heaven still has the final move.
So today ask yourself:
Am I trusting God’s timing like Esther?
Am I standing in quiet integrity like Mordecai?
Or is pride quietly building gallows in my own heart?
The Gospel calls us to lay down pride, turn from sin, and trust the One who turned the cross into victory.
Because in God’s kingdom…
The plan of evil never gets the final word.
Grace does.
And in Christ, every story can still be rewritten.
THE PLAN BACKFIRED.
God reverses injustice.
And through Jesus, He can reverse your story too.
Someone you know might need this reminder today.
